title: Release-feedback processing performs repeated GT/session and stage-max queries in an N+1 pattern

original_titles.title: release_feedback is N+1: one gt session per submission plus repeated stage-max queries

problem: The release_feedback handler processes submissions and performs repeated ground-truth lookups/session creation and repeated stage-max computations while applying release penalties/defaults. This increases DB round trips as submission volume grows.
impact: A release operation can become slow or hold locks/resources for too long under a larger participant count, increasing event-day release latency.

verification.basis: Current source inspection at the main-branch commit listed in metadata. Original audit line numbers are treated as historical and were not reused as current line references.

implementation_steps.action: Profile query count and wall-clock time for 50/200/500 submissions using realistic DB data. Record baseline p95.
Fetch all candidate bug points and relevant stage configuration in bounded batch queries before processing submissions.
Compute stage max once per stage and reuse it; avoid opening a GT session inside each submission loop.
Apply ledger writes in bounded batches while preserving transaction/idempotency boundaries.
Add a query-count regression test and a load test for result release.

acceptance_criteria: Query count grows sub-linearly or near-constant with submissions per stage.
Release completes under the approved event cap within the agreed deadline.
regression_tests: Add a focused failing test before implementation where practical.
Add a negative authorization / boundary test, not only a happy-path test.
Run the affected backend/frontend suite and the full CI workflow before merge.
